presentation.label: SCOPE
presentation.summary: A live oscilloscope of your signal on the pedal screen: the waveform, or left against right.
presentation.overview: Scope draws the signal coming into its slot across the whole screen, up to about 30 times a second, and passes the audio through untouched. Time spreads the trace from 3 to 186 ms across the screen, Gain zooms in up to 32 times, and Mode switches between the waveform and an XY view of left against right.
highlights: The signal at its place in the chain, full screen
usage: Put Scope in a patch right after the effect you want to see.
Play: your signal draws across the screen. Time spreads it out, Gain zooms in.
Set Mode to 1 to see left against right (XY).

access.location: The pedal's effect list, Delay group, as Scope.
steps: Add Scope to a patch from the effect list (Delay group).
Its knobs are on the effect's pages, three per page.

controls.name: Time
controls.doc: Time across the screen: 1 to 64 samples per column (2.9 to 186 ms).

limitations: Its live screen needs the MS-70CDR 2.10.
Built with the init path off: a recalled patch plays the knobs' defaults until you touch a knob.

load.conditions: The cost Scope declares in its descriptor, which the pedal adds up per patch; not read from the DSP meter.

hardware.summary: The release file was on the pedal (read back over USB with the same SHA-256): the pedal booted, the effect showed its screen and did its job.
limitations: One run, reported by the tester as working; nothing measured.
Built with the init path off: the sound takes saved knob values only once a knob is touched.
MIDISTOMP V2.0.1 on Zoom's 2.10, not Zoom's 2.10 alone.

tests.summary: The release file has no code from Zoom's effects (check_no_stock.py), passes Ziddle's loader check, renders in Ziddle, and ran on an MS-70CDR.
